# Reviewed judgment routes the one door does not own.
#
# Standing law 2: all judgment routes through kernel admission, and a private
# validator is a second door. `check:kernel-door` reads every `admit` route
# under `packages/plait/src/` — exported or not, because a private validator is
# the shape the law names — and requires each one to BE the door's own function.
# A module that names a route the door does not own is written here, by hand,
# with the ticket that owns its convergence.
#
# This file is nothing's input. Adding a row is the whole cost of the exception
# and is the diff a reviewer reads; a row that stops naming a real route reds
# the wall rather than rotting, so the roster cannot outlive what it waives.
#
# Format: <module path relative to packages/plait> <ticket>
#
# src/planes/Address.ts — the petname name law. It accepts no candidate,
# constructs no verdict, and teaches no kernel refusal; what it mints is this
# module's own `invalid-petname`, which the module header already stages as
# DEV-796 debt beside `Binding` and `Directory`. The row records that the
# package spells a second admission somewhere, and names the ticket that
# converges it, rather than letting the name pass unread.
src/planes/Address.ts DEV-796
